frequency_question: How often do bilateral transboundary water treaties successfully get replaced or renewed prior to expiration when formal advance signaling is mixed or absent?
membership_rule: Includes any bilateral or multilateral transboundary water-sharing treaty approaching expiration where renewal or renegotiation was formally initiated. Excludes cases terminated by military conflict or unilateral withdrawal without negotiation.

cases.name: US-Canada Columbia River Treaty regime reviews and modernization talks
Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase II implementation agreements
Senegal River Basin Development Organization (OMVS) protocol renewals
India-Pakistan Indus Waters Treaty continuous operational modifications/dispute mechanisms

coverage_note: 4 named major cases representing distinct structural categories of transboundary water treaty renewals.
known_gaps: Transboundary water negotiations often occur behind closed diplomatic channels with sparse public data on minor basin agreements.
skeleton: Global instances of expiring water treaties over a 30-year span, categorized by whether high-level joint committee frameworks were actively meeting in the final 24 months before expiration.
multiplier: 4 observed major negotiations; 2 resulted in formal signed successor instruments or formal protocols before or immediately at deadline, 2 lapsed into prolonged indefinite talks without signed instruments.
validity_reason: International water law frameworks and riparian negotiation dynamics remain stable over multi-year horizons.
